newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-INDIA CRAWL TO 161-4 AT TEA V S.LANKA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIA CRAWL TO 161-4 AT TEA V S.LANKA.

text.p: Indian batsman Mohammad Azharuddin became a stumbling block for Sri Lanka as they pressed for a win in the second and final test at Colombo on Wednesday.
India, content to survive instead of chasing a victory target of 373 runs, were 161 for four wickets at tea, still requiring 212 off a possible 33 overs in the final session.
Former captain Azharuddin was fortunate to be unbeaten on 40 and Sri Lanka will need to remove him quickly to have any chance of winning.

Azharuddin has already survived two chances, one a return catch to off-spinner Muttiah Muralitharan. Wicketkeeper Romesh Kaluwitharana put down the other chance off left-arm spinner Sanatha Jayasuriya.
During the afternoon session Sri Lanka picked up the wickets of captain Sachin Tendulkar and Ajay Jadeja, who has top scored in the innings so far.
Jadeja, who made 73 in 254 minutes off 176 balls with eight fours, was caught by Marvan Atapattu at gully off the bowling of Sajeeva de Silva.
Earlier, Tendulkar at eight attempted to loft Muralitharan and gave an easy catch to de Silva at mid-on.
India managed 67 runs in the afternoon session after scoring a mere 45 in the morning, when two wickets also fell following their resumption on 49 without loss.
Chaminda Vaas snapped up the wicket of Navjot Sidhu, who edged a catch to Jayasuriya at second slip when he had made 16.
Rahul Dravid hung around for 69 minutes and scored only six before Muralitharan pushed one through quickly to have him caught off bat and pad by Atapattu at forward short-leg.
